scope: Client-side grammar and carrier closure for the typed actor-property stream. Names and values describe client/capture evidence only and do not claim server behavior.

grammar.runningByteTotal: u8 at application +0; parsing is bounded to min(136, 1 + runningByteTotal)
grammar.termination: A zero lead byte terminates the stream; the declared running-byte bound is an independent hard stop.

propertyRecord.shape: u8 valueWidth, u32 propertyHash little-endian, valueWidth raw value bytes
propertyRecord.typeBoundary: The lead byte proves payload width. Width 1/2/4 is compatible with scalar storage, but the wire alone does not distinguish signedness or int32 from float32. Width 11/95 remains an opaque buffer.
propertyRecord.hashIdentity: The u32 hash identifies the complete property path. Array indices are ASCII bracket suffixes inside the hashed candidate string, not separate wire fields; for example castGauge_speed[0] and castGauge_speed[1] hash independently.

targetMarker.shape: u8 marker followed by the marker-family decoded number of printable ASCII bytes; it changes the active target for following property records
targetMarker.ranges: 0x60..0x9f and 0xa4..0xe3 are marker families decoded by the retained corpus parser; decoded length is marker-0x60 below 0x82, marker-0x82 from 0x82..0x9f, or marker-0xa4 from 0xa4..0xe3.
targetMarker.boundary: Target strings are capture-observed stream context. They do not alter the property hash or encode an array index.

derivation: xivl-decomp:asm/ffxivgame/00375180_FUN_00775180.s:0x00775264-0x00775679 - client parser consumes one lead byte, branches across marker ranges, advances by decoded marker length, and applies registry records.
xivl-captures:tools/extractors/extract_gam_keys.py:parse_property_block - deterministic corpus grammar and width/hash/value extraction.
manifests/gam_hash_names.json and tools/verify_murmur2.py - exact backward MurmurHash2 matches, including indexed names.

carriers.name: SetActorPropertyPacket
carriers.derivation: The mapped 0x0137 dispatcher reaches SyncMemoryReceiver apply FUN_0089E550, which calls FUN_00775A30 and then FUN_00775180.

nonCarrierCallers: FUN_00775890 reaches FUN_00775180 from client-local registry/state iteration; its callers FUN_006E17E0 and FUN_006E1F70 are not packet dispatcher cases.
carrierClosure.conclusion: No second dispatcher opcode feeding the identical typed stream was found in the retained client route. The catalog therefore covers s2c 0x0137 only.

hashDerivation.algorithm: seed-0 backward MurmurHash2 over the canonical property path

factoryDispatch.arraySelection: ArrayInformation selects by element Information subtype and the partial-array branch.

registryPopulation.insertPair: u32 property hash -> writer handler owning the selected concrete SyncWriter

handlerSurface.raw: FUN_00CFD610 registers the concrete writer directly when the shared-work-type sentinel is -2.
handlerSurface.wrapped: Otherwise FUN_00CFD610 registers a SyncWriterWithSharedWorkType adapter whose inner concrete writer is at +0x04.
handlerSurface.applyDispatch: The adapter's vtable slot 1 forwards to inner-writer vtable slot 1.

registryPopulation.conclusion: Construction and apply use the same ActorWorkSync +0x0C tree. The path hash selects a handler object whose concrete SyncWriter class is chosen by the field's Information subtype, not a fixed actor-structure offset.

pendingStream.replay: FUN_00775890 replays each pending record through FUN_00775180, then FUN_00786C70 destroys the record vector and erases the map node.

applyStorageBoundary.boundary: The construction and apply paths close hash-to-writer-handler population and concrete writer selection. Writer-local storage remains distinct from CharaBase and PlayerBase; no fixed actor field offset is claimed.

indexConvention.rule: Every positive Lua array index is decremented by one before the canonical path is built. Lua index 1 therefore hashes with suffix [0], and hash suffix [5] addresses Lua index 6.

properties.storageTarget: writer-local array state: extent at writer+0x10 and vector storage rooted at writer+0x18; no fixed actor field offset
properties.consumerBoundary: Decoded Lua getStateMainSkill returns state_mainSkill[1] and [2], and other Lua consumers pass those tokens to skill-category and battle-class helpers. No direct native consumer establishes a class/job identifier namespace.

properties.storageTarget: writer-local integer16 at writer+0x10; no fixed actor field offset
properties.consumerBoundary: Decoded Lua getStateMainSkillLevel returns this scalar and level-adjustment code consumes it as a level. No separate native backing-field consumer was found.

properties.storageTarget: writer-local endian-adjusted short array: extent at writer+0x10 and vector storage rooted at writer+0x18; no fixed actor field offset
properties.consumerBoundary: Decoded Lua getPhysicalParameter(n) reads generalParameter[n+3]. The bonus-point widget labels n=2 as vitCurrent and n=3 as dexCurrent, so native index 5 reaches the latter Lua display projection, not the former. These labels are Lua/display evidence, not a native gameplay namespace; no direct native consumer names this element.
No battleTemp.hpMax descriptor or observed property hash exists in the retained catalog. The registry chain cannot select a writer for this unregistered exact path.

calibrationCorrection.storageTarget: writer-local endian-adjusted short array: extent at writer+0x10 and vector storage rooted at writer+0x18; no fixed actor field offset
calibrationCorrection.consumerBoundary: Decoded Lua getHPMax calls getPartsHPMax with Lua index 1, which reaches getHpMaxImpl and parameterSave.hpMax[1]. CharaBase initialization also binds token 1011 to charaWork.parameterSave.hpMax. This proves the HP-maximum script/binding domain, not a fixed C++ actor field.

evidenceRuns.result: Verified COMPLETE export: zero defined-string matches for battleTemp, generalParameter, hpMax, parameterSave, state_mainSkill, and state_mainSkillLevel among 28,414 defined strings. This excludes only Ghidra-recorded exact defined strings and does not exclude computed or script-loaded names.

playerHpWriterIdentity.conclusion: The four requested strings do not all name registered properties. Three exact hashes select writer-local typed handlers with a proven Lua-to-native array-index shift. The requested battleTemp.hpMax[0] path is absent; the HP calibration property is parameterSave.hpMax[0]. No direct native consumer promotes state_mainSkill[0] to a class/job id or generalParameter[5] to Vitality.

catalog.resolutionRule: Every promoted name exactly matches backward MurmurHash2 with seed 0. Similarity and contextual inference are excluded.
catalog.arrayIndexRule: Bracket indices are part of the ASCII hash input. The castGauge_speed[0]/[1] pair hashes to distinct observed ids 0x573fe04c/0xbb9cc775.

epochProbe.obstruction: The two retained deadline rows alone do not establish a clock representation. Independent native evidence now proves that worldMaster._getServerTime returns the NetworkModule whole-second field and that castEndClient is an absolute deadline in that same Unix-compatible clock domain.
epochProbe.boundary: The property-row study remains insufficient by itself; the promoted whole-second absolute-deadline claim comes from xivl-decomp:docs/actor/cast-timing-clock.md at commit 51f908e6a963b7e4a33cdb3f1b9b2f3573ef31df.
